title: EU activates the Temporary Protection Directive for people fleeing Ukraine
body:
The European Union activated its Temporary Protection Directive for people fleeing the war in Ukraine in March 2022. The European Commission proposed invoking the directive on 2 March 2022. EU interior ministers agreed unanimously on 3 March 2022, and the Council of the European Union formally activated the mechanism on 4 March 2022.

The directive gives people displaced from Ukraine a residence permit in EU member states without requiring them to go through an individual asylum procedure. Holders of temporary protection may work and may access social welfare. Children are entitled to access education on the same terms as residents of the host country. The protection applies throughout the European Union, which allowed people arriving through Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Hungary and other border states to move on to other member states.

Temporary protection under the directive can last up to three years depending on circumstances. According to the Wikipedia article on the directive, on 26 June 2026 the European Commission formally proposed extending protection for people from Ukraine until March 2028; that article does not say whether the proposal has been adopted. UNHCR's statistics on refugees from Ukraine in EU countries rely on temporary protection counts compiled by Eurostat, which makes the directive a central source of the figures cited in later reporting on the scale of the displacement.
